plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated threshold workout for speed development.
Features a longer, trail-specific endurance run.
Incorporates cross-training for varied movement and recovery.
plan_b_advantages: More consistent aerobic volume with longer runs.
Tempo run is included, providing a direct speed stimulus (though less targeted than Plan A’s threshold work).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a dedicated threshold workout, crucial for building the sustainable strength needed for faster paces on trails, alongside a longer, more trail-specific endurance run. Plan B, while including a tempo run, relies heavily on consistent, longer aerobic runs which, while beneficial for endurance, don't directly target the speed improvements desired. The inclusion of a cross-training session in Plan A also provides a valuable opportunity for varied movement and recovery, complementing the other workouts effectively.  Plan A’s structured approach to building a stronger aerobic base and incorporating a specific speed-focused workout is more targeted to the athlete's goal.
